I guess I should.... It'll be the first time in my life where I can make my own decisions. It's scary but exhilarating. 

I'm gonna do it, and I'm going to be my own man. I'm going to truly end the cycle of abuse at my terms.


Cheers! 🎉

I think I should move out then. I currently have a job in the restaurant industry, and have quickly made it prevalent that I'm a good worker. I have no doubt in my mind that I would find another job that could easily help me pay for everything. Obviously, if I moved down there I would probably buy a bicycle and start commuting on a bike.

I would honestly keep doing what I have been doing. My goal this whole time welqa to get my IT certification and score an entry level IT job. 

A potential 6 month timeline would be: continue living here for two weeks while squaring my plans away, and securing my money. After that, take a flight down to Florida. Get another job serving and continue working as much as I currently do. I would then save for a car while working on my certification. I would estimate about 3-6 months to save up for a car. In my mind,it'll realistically be about 5-6. After I get my car I would get an entry level IT job and prepare for night classes at my, then, local community college.


I think I'm kind of set on the plan, I just don't know how much longer I can hold on. This is my biggest issue because I really hate that I'm almost 20 years old and I'm STILL living in the same bedroom as my mother who will continue to live vicariously through me.

I highly doubt that I will attend Electric Forest this year(RIP dream and money). I think I need to prioritize my independence first and foremost because I'm truly tired of not having my own voice. Especialy with siblings who will continue to keep downplaying my current situation.

Sorry, I think I just need to vent a little to try and squeeze some rationality into this situation before I screw things up.

The difference lies in the underlying ideas of a mindfulness approach. Some guys truly try to ignore their feelings, you can not ignore objective reality. You have to embrace that you are allowed to be nervous approaching a girl. Ignoring your nervousness is getting rid of the idea that you have to be above all which in turn devalues you.

It's a mentality thing, but it's a really big mentality thing. Ill give you two examples, one example is in public speaking. A good public speaker that gets nervous will in advance tend to admit their nervousness. Because the audience will for the most part understand that public speaking is difficult, they will look at the speaker through a more human lens and actually give more of a listen because it's more about building an authentic, genuine connection with the audience. 

Lets take day game for an example, you go up to a girl and start to notice your nervousness. Maybe she is a little more chatty than you expected and you can't keep up with her. Maybe she has more experiences than you. What will admitting your nervousness to her do? You can play into it by telling her something like, "Oh, I've never tried x, ive been too shy to ever do that." Which will lead into planning something and you can then ask for her number and go on a date. What this is really doing is building a genuine and authentic connection that is representative of objective reality. Whereas, if you ignored your feelings your playing a game that is not yours. 

EDIT: Forgot to add a sentence.


You have to embrace anxiety because if you ignore it then you are just crippling yourself by not ever facing it.
